subject: Follow-up: Incident response / SLA expectations - NimbleOps evaluation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Incident response / SLA expectations - NimbleOps evaluation

Ben/Alexa — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

1) Top priorities you called out
- Predictable latency under load (p95 target ~200ms for interactive features)
- Clear incident response process & RCA timelines after sev incidents
- Data isolation and auditability for compliance reviews

2) Where Redwood maps to those priorities (high level)
- Serving runtime built for low p95 across multi-tenant and dedicated modes
- SLA tiers available for Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity) and options for SLO-driven alerts + incident playbooks
- Audit logs, KMS integrations, and Private deployment options

3) Immediate asks / next tests we proposed on call
- Short controlled stress test (1000 r/s sustained for 10 minutes) to measure p95 and cold-start behavior
- Failure injection scenario to validate fallback routing across regions/variants
- Review of incident/RCA cadence and examples from other customers (you asked specifically about competitor outages)

I've attached a short comparison doc that contrasts Redwood SLAs and incident response practices vs common hyperscaler/inference APIs. If you can share a little more detail on the recent outage you referenced (timeline / impact / expected RCA cadence), I can tailor the follow-up and pull in our reliability folks. 

Proposed next step: 30-minute tech review + test scoping next week. Your availability?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Incident response / SLA expectations - NimbleOps evaluation

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the doc. Helpful. 

Quick color on the outage we mentioned on the call: 
- Date/time: 2026-10-28 09:12–09:47 PT
- Impact: 18 minutes of elevated latency followed by a partial 503 spike for one of our inference routes; degraded UX for internal alpha users
- Root cause per provider: "control plane failover + cache warmup" — our ask to vendors was for a faster RCA and a clear mitigation plan to avoid repeated customer impact.

What we care most about for vendor comparisons:
- How quickly do you provide an initial incident summary (timeline + customer impact)? 24 hours? 72 hours?
- When do you provide a full RCA with remediation items? We want an expected SLA for that deliverable.
- Do you have playbooks for cache-warmup / KV cache rehydration and cross-region fallback?

I can share a short timeline (we have internal logs) if that helps. Also curious about the failure injection + warmup test you suggested — would you run that on our account or provide a test harness?

-Ben
Ben Harper
Director of Platform Engineering | NimbleOps
ben.harper@nimbleops.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-14T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Incident response / SLA expectations - NimbleOps evaluation

Ben — really useful context, thanks. Short answers + proposed path forward below.

1) Incident summary timing (initial)
- Redwood provides an initial incident summary within 4 business hours for Sev 1/2 incidents for customers on Dedicated with SLA contracts; for hosted accounts we target 8 business hours for initial updates. The initial summary includes timeline, affected routes, and immediate mitigation steps.

2) Full RCA timeline
- For SLA-backed Dedicated customers we commit to a preliminary RCA within 72 hours and a final RCA (with remediation items and regression tests) within 14 calendar days. For hosted customers we scope on a case-by-case basis; we can also offer an accelerated path in contract for >72h preliminary RCAs.

3) Playbooks / cache warmup
- We have documented playbooks for KV cache rehydration and progressive traffic ramping; playbooks include: priority warmup keys, staged traffic routing, and throttled cache-fill to avoid origin overload. We can share the RCA-template (attached) that shows the standard artifacts we produce post-incident.

4) Failure injection + warmup test
- Two options:
  a) Redwood-run controlled test (we run the harness against a dedicated test pool we provision for you) — recommended for the full end-to-end validation.
  b) Self-run harness + runbook (we provide scripts and runbook) — lower-touch and lets your team own scheduling.
We typically include KV warmup validation, cold-start metrics, and cross-region failover timing in the test scope.

Next steps I propose:
- I will schedule a 30-minute tech scoping session where Vivek (reliability) and Rishi (support/SLAs) can explain the playbooks and walk through our failure-injection options.
- I'll attach the SLA comparison and RCA template for your legal/ops review.

Can we do Wednesday 11/18 10am PT for the scoping call? If that doesn't work, propose two windows.

Thanks — looping in the reliability folks to prep notes.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachment: RCA-template.docx

- Rishi: please confirm the SLA language we offer for preliminary and final RCAs for Dedicated customers and whether we have an expedited option for hosted accounts (include timeline and any contract triggers).
- Laura: attach two anonymized RCAs (redacted) that show format and remediation tracking — prefer examples that include cache warmup mitigations.
